    Interval representations of the linearly oriented quiver #

    The representations of 1 → 2 → ⋯ → n are the functors Fin n ⥤ FGModuleCat k (Statement.LinRep). For a ≤ d in Fin n, the interval representation interval k a d (Definition 5.1, M_{a,d} in the manuscript) is k at the vertices of [a, d], zero elsewhere, with identity maps inside the interval. It is realized with the submodule of k that is ⊤ on [a, d] and ⊥ outside, so that all vertex spaces have one uniform type; every structure map is "the inclusion if it exists, zero otherwise" (inclusionOrZero), whose value in k is given by coe_inclusionOrZero.

    This file gives the construction and its basic API: values and maps at the vertices, the canonical inclusions interval k ℓ d ⟶ interval k a d and projections interval k a d ⟶ interval k a ℓ, and the dimension of the vertex spaces.
